name: Zhipu AI
h1: Zhipu AI ARR: $1.6B Annualized and the First Chinese Lab Past $1B.
intro: Zhipu AI (Z.ai) went from roughly $100M to a $1B annualized run rate in about five months, then reported an August 2026 run rate near $1.6B after its Hong Kong IPO. Every reported revenue figure below is traced to a public source — mostly earnings filings and 36Kr.

modelTitle: How Discounted GLM Tokens Buy the Volume.
modelParagraphs: Zhipu monetizes primarily through GLM API usage: developers pay per million tokens, with flag-ship GLM models priced at steep discounts to Western labs — historically on the order of $0.10–$0.60 per million input tokens. Enterprise contracts (finance, telecom, government SOEs) add licensing and private-deployment deals, and the consumer-facing Z.ai chatbot carries subscription tiers.

The economics are still aggressive: H1 2026 carried roughly 24.6% margins while the company spent heavily on compute, and FY2025 closed with a ~RMB 4.7B loss. The bet is that China's lowest-cost frontier API wins volume — J.P. Morgan expects adjusted profit only by 2028.

faqs.q: What Is Zhipu AI's ARR in 2026?
faqs.a: Zhipu AI (Z.ai) reached roughly $1 billion in annualized revenue by July 2026, and annualizing August revenue implies about $1.6 billion — around $133 million of monthly run rate. Figures convert RMB filings and press reports; the August number is an annualization, not an audited ARR.

faqs.q: How Fast Did Zhipu AI Grow?
faqs.a: From a ~$67M annualized run rate in February 2026 to $1B by July — about five months for the final $100M-to-$1B leg per Bloomberg. H1 2026 revenue quintupled year over year.

faqs.q: What Does Zhipu AI Actually Sell?
faqs.a: Mostly GLM API access billed per token at some of the lowest frontier-model prices in the market, plus private enterprise deployments for Chinese finance, telecom and state-owned customers, and consumer subscriptions to the Z.ai chatbot.

No. FY2025 closed with a ~RMB 4.7 billion (~$683M) net loss despite revenue growing 132%, though H1 2026 losses narrowed as revenue quintupled. J.P. Morgan analysts model adjusted profitability by 2028.
The stock trades on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under ticker 2513.HK, with a market capitalization around $92 billion in 2026 after a post-IPO share price surge of roughly 2,000%.
